label: Constituency
plain_definition: A geographical area whose voters together elect a fixed number of TDs to the Dail. Ireland currently has 43 of them.
formal_definition: A geographical subdivision of a state created to provide its population with representation in the legislature; in Ireland, a grouping of electoral divisions returning 3 to 5 TDs.
why_it_matters: The constituency is the unit whose lines redistricting redraws; where the lines fall decides whose votes are pooled together and how much each vote weighs.

label: Dail Eireann
plain_definition: The national parliament of Ireland, whose members are elected from constituencies.
formal_definition: Dail Eireann is the directly elected house of the Oireachtas; its total membership is fixed by law within the bounds set by Article 16.2.2 of the Constitution.
why_it_matters: Everything in this course is ultimately about who sits in the Dail and whether voters are represented there evenly.

label: Teachta Dala (TD)
plain_definition: An elected member of the Dail. Each constituency elects 3, 4 or 5 TDs.
formal_definition: A Teachta Dala is a member of Dail Eireann returned by a constituency at a general election or by-election.
why_it_matters: Representation is counted in TDs: people-per-TD is the yardstick for electoral fairness used throughout the pipeline.

label: County
plain_definition: One of Ireland's 26 traditional administrative regions, each governed by a county council. Constituency lines are supposed to respect county lines where practicable.
formal_definition: An administrative region of Ireland governed by a county council; constituency boundaries are legally independent of county boundaries but conformity is a statutory consideration.
why_it_matters: People identify with their county; breaching county lines is one of the most contested aspects of any boundary change and one of the objectives the algorithm must weigh.

label: Proportional representation (PR)
plain_definition: The idea that the mix of parties elected should mirror the mix of support among voters.
formal_definition: An electoral system in which the underlying distribution of electorate support for each political party is reflected proportionately in the elected representative body.
why_it_matters: PR motivates the whole pipeline: as population shifts, boundaries must move to keep representation even. The paper calls redistricting a necessary consequence of PR.

label: PR-STV (single transferable vote)
plain_definition: The Irish voting method: you rank candidates 1, 2, 3 and so on, and if your first choice is elected with votes to spare or is eliminated, your vote can move on to your next choice.
formal_definition: Article 16.2.5 of the Constitution requires that Dail members be elected on a system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote in multi-member constituencies.
why_it_matters: The paper assumes this background. Without PR-STV you cannot see why multi-seat constituencies exist at all, or why their size and shape affect proportionality.

label: Quota (Droop quota)
plain_definition: The number of votes that guarantees a candidate a seat: the total valid vote divided by one more than the number of seats, plus one (fractions ignored).
formal_definition: Droop quota = floor(total valid poll / (seats + 1)) + 1, the smallest number such that no more than the available number of seats can reach it.
why_it_matters: Explains how STV counts actually decide winners, and why more seats per constituency lowers the bar for smaller parties to win a seat.

label: Vote transfers
plain_definition: When a candidate is elected with a surplus over the quota, or eliminated for having fewest votes, their ballots move to the next preference still in the race.
formal_definition: Under PR-STV, surpluses of elected candidates and all votes of eliminated candidates are redistributed according to next available preferences until all seats are filled.
why_it_matters: Transfers are what makes STV proportional in practice; they are the mechanism through which constituency composition shapes who ultimately wins seats.

label: Seat magnitude (3-5 seats)
plain_definition: How many TDs a constituency elects. Irish law currently allows only 3, 4 or 5.
formal_definition: The Electoral Reform Act 2022 (terms of reference, item 2) requires each constituency to return 3, 4 or 5 members; the paper also cites the Electoral Act 1997 for the set {3,4,5}.
why_it_matters: Seat magnitude fixes the allowed population sizes of constituencies, drives the min-over-m structure of H_P, and controls the proportionality-versus-locality trade-off.

label: Electoral redistricting
plain_definition: Redrawing the boundary lines that define constituencies, mainly by moving small areas from one constituency to another as population changes.
formal_definition: The process of redrawing the electoral boundaries that make up constituencies; in Ireland, effected by transferring electoral divisions between constituencies and by changing the number of constituencies.
why_it_matters: This is the activity the entire COTHROM framework automates and audits; every later concept exists to do this task well.

label: An Coimisiun Toghchain (Electoral Commission)
plain_definition: The independent state body, established on 9 February 2023, that oversees elections and reviews Dail constituency boundaries.
formal_definition: A statutory body whose functions include reviewing Dail constituencies after each census and reporting recommendations for boundary changes, subject to the Constitution and terms of reference.
why_it_matters: It is the human decision-maker the algorithmic framework is designed to support, not replace.

label: Constituency review
plain_definition: The periodic process, run after each census, in which a commission examines population change and recommends new constituency boundaries in a published report.
formal_definition: A statutory review of Dail constituencies conducted after each census, historically by ad hoc Constituency Commissions (reports 1980-2017) and since 2023 by the Electoral Commission.
why_it_matters: The review reports are the real-world outputs the framework aims to make faster, more transparent and more testable; their history (Table 1) is the evidence base for how rules were applied.

label: Constitutional provisions (Article 16.2)
plain_definition: The Constitution requires roughly one TD for every 20,000 to 30,000 people nationally, and, as far as practicable, the same ratio of TDs to population in every constituency.
formal_definition: Article 16.2.2: total Dail membership between one member per 30,000 and one per 20,000 of population. Article 16.2.3: the ratio of members to population, per the last census, shall so far as practicable be the same throughout the country.
why_it_matters: These are the unbreakable legal anchors of the whole problem: they define both the size of the Dail and the equal-representation standard every metric tries to capture.

label: Terms of reference (Electoral Reform Act 2022, s.57)
plain_definition: The statutory rules a review must observe: 171-181 TDs in total, 3-5 seats per constituency, constituencies in one piece, and due regard to county boundaries, geography and continuity with existing boundaries.
formal_definition: Section 57 of the Electoral Reform Act 2022: (1) 171-181 members; (2) 3, 4 or 5 seats each; (3) county boundaries preserved as far as practicable; (4) contiguity; (5) geographic considerations; (6) continuity of existing arrangements.
why_it_matters: This is the rule set the algorithm must encode. The paper notes items (1), (2) and (4) cannot be broken while (3), (5) and (6) can and will be transgressed to some extent.

label: Gerrymandering
plain_definition: Drawing boundaries deliberately to favour a party or group, named after Elbridge Gerry and the salamander-shaped district he approved.
formal_definition: The deliberate manipulation of electoral boundaries to advantage or disadvantage a political interest, classically detectable in highly non-compact district shapes.
why_it_matters: It is the failure mode boundary rules exist to prevent, the historical motivation for compactness measures, and a stress test the framework can run against proposed rule sets.

label: Census population data
plain_definition: The official population counts from the Central Statistics Office census, which every review must work from.
formal_definition: Population as ascertained at the last preceding census (Article 16.2.3), published by the CSO down to small-area level; updated census data is the input that triggers and drives each review.
why_it_matters: Population change is the engine of the whole problem: it is what makes yesterday's fair map unfair today.

label: Electoral division (ED)
plain_definition: One of the 3,440 small areas Ireland is divided into. EDs are the building blocks: boundaries change by moving whole EDs between constituencies.
formal_definition: The smallest geographic units used in the redistricting problem; each ED carries a population and a list of neighbours. Note the CSO reports some data at the level of CSO EDs, which differ slightly from EDs.
why_it_matters: If you know your ED you can trace exactly how any proposed boundary change affects you; algorithmically, EDs are the atoms every configuration is built from.

label: Map (building-block view)
plain_definition: The whole territory seen as a bag of building blocks (the EDs) with their population data attached, before any constituency lines are drawn on it.
formal_definition: The Map is the collection of districts (building blocks) that make up the region to be redistricted; in the Irish case the map is the Republic and the blocks are EDs.
why_it_matters: Separating the fixed map from the movable lines is the first abstraction of the paper's framework: reviews change boundaries, never the map itself.

label: Graph (nodes and edges)
plain_definition: A mathematical picture made of dots (nodes) joined by lines (edges), used to record which things are connected to which.
formal_definition: A graph G = (V, E) is a set of vertices V and a set of edges E, each edge joining a pair of vertices.
why_it_matters: Almost every technical step - contiguity checks, compactness counts, county-breach counts, the Potts lattice - works on a graph rather than on the physical map.

label: ED adjacency graph
plain_definition: A graph with one node per ED and an edge wherever two EDs share a land border. It is the algorithm's entire picture of Irish geography.
formal_definition: The graph whose vertices are the 3,440 EDs and whose edges join land-connected EDs, built from the CSO GeoDataFrame; county and community boundaries are overlaid as labelled edges.
why_it_matters: Once geography is a graph, legal ideas like contiguous and compact become computable, and the search can restrict moves to genuinely neighbouring areas.

label: Split (non-contiguous) EDs
plain_definition: Four EDs are themselves split into pieces that do not touch. The algorithm treats each whole ED as one connected node, which the paper calls a fine approximation.
formal_definition: Exceptions to the land-connected definition of neighbouring EDs; when each ED is absorbed into a single graph node these divisions are treated as land-connected.
why_it_matters: An honest caveat: the tidy graph slightly idealises the messy map, and readers should know where the idealisation lives.

label: Configuration
plain_definition: One complete possible answer: a label on every ED saying which constituency it belongs to.
formal_definition: A function assigning each of the 3,440 EDs to exactly one of Q constituencies; equivalently one composition of Dail constituencies and their boundaries.
why_it_matters: The configuration is the object everything else acts on: metrics score it, algorithms mutate it, and the final recommendation is one of them.

label: Rule set
plain_definition: The list of criteria that decides whether a proposed map counts as valid - the legal rules written down in a form you can actually check.
formal_definition: The codification of a system's aspirations for its boundaries; applied to a Map it partitions candidate configurations into valid and invalid ones.
why_it_matters: The paper's central claim is that your interpretation of the rules is encoded in the boundaries you accept, so the rule set must be explicit and checkable rather than implicit.

label: Boundaries (a valid set of constituencies)
plain_definition: A full set of constituencies that satisfies the rule set for a given map. Crucially, many different valid Boundaries usually exist for the same rules.
formal_definition: A collection of constituencies that meets the rule set criteria for a specific Map; multiple valid boundary configurations can exist within a given rule set framework.
why_it_matters: That validity does not pin down a unique answer is the key fact: it creates the selection problem of which valid map to recommend.

label: Solution space (combinatorial explosion)
plain_definition: The collection of all possible ways to assign EDs to constituencies - a number so large no human or computer could ever list them all.
formal_definition: The set of all configurations; the paper notes S(3440, Q) exceeds 10^5000 for Q of 30 or more, with only a tiny sliver satisfying the legal requirements.
why_it_matters: The impossibility of enumeration is why sampling and optimisation are needed at all, and why claims like 'this map minimises county breaches' cannot be verified by hand.

label: National average (National Ratio)
aliases: national ratio;people per TD;national average representation
plain_definition: The census population divided by the number of Dail seats: how many people each TD represents on average. On 2022 figures: 5,149,139 people / 174 TDs = 29,593 people per TD.
formal_definition: National Ratio = recorded census population / number of Dail seats (Eq. 1).
why_it_matters: This single number is the benchmark of fairness: every constituency is judged by how far its own people-per-TD ratio departs from it.

label: Seat Equivalent Representation (SER)
plain_definition: How many seats a constituency's population deserves: its population divided by the national average per TD. A population of 118,372 has an SER of exactly 4.
formal_definition: SER = proposed population / National Ratio (Eq. 2); its unit is seats, and population = SER x National Ratio recovers the population (Eq. 5).
why_it_matters: SER recentres the debate on representation rather than raw population, and its non-integer values are precisely where misrepresentation comes from.

label: Variance from the national average (v)
plain_definition: The percentage by which a constituency departs from the national norm once whole seats are assigned: positive means more people per TD than the national average (under-represented), negative means fewer (over-represented).
formal_definition: v = (SER - assigned seats) / assigned seats (Eq. 6); a value of +0.05 is 5 percent above the national average representation.
why_it_matters: Variance is the official fairness gauge used in every review report since 1980 and the quantity the ±5 percent convention and H_P are built around.

label: The ±5 percent variance convention
plain_definition: The long-standing working rule that each constituency's variance should stay within plus or minus 5 percent. The 2023 review broke it for 15 of 43 constituencies - the most since 1995.
formal_definition: A conventional tolerance band of |v| <= 0.05 around the national average, tracked across all reports 1980-2023 (Table 1); it is a convention, not a constitutional or statutory limit.
why_it_matters: It is the concrete standard against which reviews are judged, and its 2023 erosion is the paper's motivating evidence that the current process is straining.

label: Alternative (voter-centred) variance
plain_definition: A redefinition of variance that divides by seats deserved instead of seats assigned, so that being 5 percent over and 5 percent under correspond to the same amount of misrepresentation per person.
formal_definition: v_new = (s - a) / s where s is SER and a is assigned seats; under v_new the maximally over- and under-represented populations at threshold v experience equal misrepresentation |a/p_ext - a/p| = av/p (App C).
why_it_matters: It shows that even the definition of fairness is a design choice with provable consequences - a small formula change makes the bounds mean the same thing for every voter.

label: Contiguity
plain_definition: The requirement that a constituency be a single connected piece of land, with no detached islands of territory.
formal_definition: A constituency is contiguous when its EDs form one connected group in the adjacency graph; formally G_q = 1 connected component. Contiguity is a hard requirement in the Irish context.
why_it_matters: A voter should not live in a detached fragment of a constituency centred elsewhere; algorithmically it is one of the constraints that may never be broken in a final map.

label: Compactness
plain_definition: A measure of whether a constituency has a reasonable, roughly rounded shape rather than a sprawling, snake-like one.
formal_definition: Any of several measures penalising irregular shape: convex-hull comparison, minimising external boundary ED neighbours, or maximising internal boundary ED neighbours (S2.4); in the Potts model, border length with other constituencies.
why_it_matters: Serpentine shapes are the classic fingerprint of gerrymandering; optimising compactness steers the search away from unnatural constituencies.

label: Convex hull measure
plain_definition: One way to measure compactness: wrap the constituency in the tightest convex polygon and compare; intuitive but expensive to recompute after every change.
formal_definition: The convex hull is the smallest convex polygon enclosing the constituency; compactness compares the constituency's area or shape to its hull. The paper notes cheaper edge-counting alternatives induce similar behaviour.
why_it_matters: Shows that even an intuitive criterion has multiple formalisations with different computational costs - a recurring theme of the codification problem.

label: County-boundary breach measure
plain_definition: A count of how badly a map cuts across county lines, computed from the graph edges that cross a county boundary inside a single constituency.
formal_definition: The basic measure counts edges crossing a county boundary whose two EDs are in the same constituency, minimised during search. Convention from past reports: joining two entire counties in one constituency is not a breach (App C.1).
why_it_matters: County allegiance is one of the strongest public sentiments in submissions to reviews, and how you count a breach materially changes which maps look good.

label: Community-of-interest boundaries
plain_definition: Some communities that straddle no official line still strongly object to being split; the map can mark those connections and penalise cutting them.
formal_definition: Designated graph edges that count towards a penalty when the EDs they connect are assigned to different constituencies, implemented in the same way as county boundary edges.
why_it_matters: Shows the machinery is general: any community the public or commission identifies can be protected by labelling edges, without new mathematics.

label: Continuity with existing boundaries
plain_definition: A measure of how much a proposed map disrupts the current one - how many people and EDs wake up in a different constituency.
formal_definition: Illustrative form f_C = exp(-a_c n_people - b_c n_ED), maximal at 1 when nothing changes (Eq. 8), where n_people and n_ED count people and EDs no longer in their original constituency; the paper notes this form is blind to where changes concentrate.
why_it_matters: Continuity is a statutory consideration, and voters feel churn directly; but continuity also fights the population-driven changes fairness demands.

label: Population-weighted rule-breaking
aliases: bump function;weighting breaches by people affected
plain_definition: The idea that a rule breach should be judged by how many people it affects - and, per the Commission, that transferring too few people across a county line leaves them feeling voiceless, so transfers should carry weight.
formal_definition: An optimisation function on the SER lying over a county boundary (Fig 5), near zero for tiny transfers, with a tunable bump (height, position, width) around a preferred transfer size; bump positions at symmetric values like 1/2 or 1/3 create optimisation symmetries that hinder convergence.
why_it_matters: It converts a subtle sentiment from real Commission reports into three debatable parameters, showing both the power and the difficulty of codifying legal nuance.

label: Objective (score) function
plain_definition: A single number that scores how well a whole map obeys a rule, built so the best possible score happens exactly at the maps you want.
formal_definition: A function on configurations whose extremal values occur at rule-satisfying configurations; e.g. f_PR (Eq. 7) is extremal when SER is an allowed integer 3, 4 or 5. A function that characterises error is a requisite of optimisation.
why_it_matters: This is the conceptual hinge of the course: once rules become scores, redistricting becomes a search problem that mathematics can attack.

label: Hamiltonian (energy function)
plain_definition: Physics' name for a score function: it assigns an energy to every possible state of a system, and systems settle towards low energy.
formal_definition: A function H mapping each configuration of a system to a real number (its energy); the model's dynamics and equilibrium behaviour are determined by H.
why_it_matters: The bridge into physics: a rule-breaking score and an energy are the same mathematical object, which unlocks a toolbox built over decades of statistical mechanics.

label: Potts model
plain_definition: A classic physics model: a grid of sites, each taking one of Q values (think colours), where the energy simply counts neighbouring sites whose colours differ.
formal_definition: H_Potts = -J_Potts sum over neighbour pairs of delta(s_i, s_j) (Eqs 9-10), for spins s_i taking one of Q abstract values; introduced by Renfrey Potts in 1951.
why_it_matters: It is the exact template the electoral model instantiates: the values need not be numbers, so 'constituency 1..Q' is as valid a spin set as 'red, green, blue'.

label: Ferromagnetic configuration
plain_definition: The state where every site has the same value - in the electoral analogy, the whole country as one giant constituency.
formal_definition: The configuration with s_i = s_j for all i, j, which minimises H_Potts; an antiferromagnetic configuration maximises it.
why_it_matters: Knowing what a term is minimised by tells you what it pushes towards: the compactness term alone would merge Ireland into one constituency, so other terms must push back.

label: Electoral Potts model
plain_definition: The redistricting problem rewritten in Potts language: the 3,440 EDs are the sites, the constituency labels are the Q values, and neighbouring EDs are neighbouring sites.
formal_definition: The 3,440 EDs assigned to Q constituencies are treated as lattice sites assigned to Q spin values; constituency boundaries are groupings of values and ED borders are nearest-neighbour pairs; legal requirements are encoded as separate Hamiltonian terms (after Chou and Li 2006).
why_it_matters: This is the paper's central move: once the map is a spin system, decades of statistical-physics optimisation machinery applies to Irish boundaries.

label: H_P (representation term)
plain_definition: The energy term for fair representation: for each constituency, how far its population is from the nearest allowed multiple (3, 4 or 5 times) of the average constituency population.
formal_definition:
H_P = sum over q of min over m in {m_s} of |P_q / m -

| (Eq. 11), where P_q is the population of constituency q,

is the average population per constituency, and {m_s} = {3,4,5}; minimised when P_q = m

for allowed m (Fig 13).
why_it_matters: It is the algorithmic embodiment of Article 16.2.3: configurations where any constituency's population sits between valid seat counts are pushed uphill in energy.

label: H_C (contiguity term)
plain_definition: The energy term that punishes constituencies that are in more than one piece (or assigned no territory at all).
formal_definition: H_C = sum over q of |G_q - 1| (Eq. 11), where G_q is the number of contiguous groups in constituency q; the modulus makes an empty constituency (G_q = 0) also contribute.
why_it_matters: Contiguity is unbreakable in law, so its energy term is weighted to punish severely; it is what lets the search entertain briefly-broken maps without them surviving.

label: H_D (compactness term)
plain_definition: The energy term that counts pairs of neighbouring EDs sitting in different constituencies - in effect the total internal border length of the map.
formal_definition: H_D = sum over neighbour pairs of (1 - delta(q_i, q_j)) (Eq. 11); equal to H_Potts/J_Potts plus a constant, so minimised by the ferromagnetic (single-constituency) configuration.
why_it_matters: Short borders mean chunky, non-serpentine constituencies; but taken alone this term wants one giant constituency, a vivid lesson in why objectives must be balanced.

label: H_B (county-boundary term)
plain_definition: The energy term for county breaches. The paper offers three candidate formulas because the law does not pin down what exactly counts as a breach.
formal_definition: Candidates: H(1) = sum(C_q - 1); H(2) counts split counties in multi-county constituencies via Kronecker deltas; H(3) penalises minority county proportions via (1-(2 pi_cq -1)^2), where C_q is the number of counties in constituency q and pi_cq the proportion of county c in q. The paper does not name these H_B or choose among them.
why_it_matters: A live example of legal ambiguity becoming a modelling decision: which formula you pick is an interpretation of the law, and it changes the resulting maps.

label: Coupling constants (J_alpha)
plain_definition: The dial attached to each rule's energy term, setting how much that rule matters relative to the others. The law provides no values for these dials.
formal_definition: The weights J_alpha in H = sum of J_alpha H_alpha (Eq. 12). There is no a priori way to compute them from a desired hierarchy, effects are not linear in the weights, and only ratios matter: scaling all J_alpha and T by the same factor changes nothing, so one may set J_P = 1 (S5.1.1).
why_it_matters: The coupling constants are where value judgements hide inside the mathematics; making them explicit is what makes the algorithm auditable and debatable.

label: Total Hamiltonian H = sum of J_alpha H_alpha
plain_definition: The single overall energy of a map: each rule's term multiplied by its weight, all added up. Redistricting becomes: find the map with the lowest total energy.
formal_definition: H = sum over alpha of J_alpha H_alpha (Eq. 12), alpha ranging over requirements P, C, D, and so on; the redistricting problem reduces to choosing {J_alpha} and finding configurations minimising H.
why_it_matters: This one line is the entire reframing: a centuries-old civic problem compressed into a function that a computer can minimise and a citizen can inspect term by term.

label: Temperature (T)
plain_definition: A knob controlling how willing the search is to accept changes that make the map worse: high temperature means adventurous exploration, low temperature means strict improvement only.
formal_definition: The parameter T in the Boltzmann weight exp(-H/T) (Eq. 13, with k_B = 1); high T approaches uniform random sampling of configurations, low T restricts sampling to near a local extremum (S4.2.1).
why_it_matters: Temperature is what separates a naive greedy search that gets stuck from a search that can escape bad neighbourhoods of the solution space.

label: Boltzmann distribution
plain_definition: A probability rule that prefers low-energy maps: each map's chance is weighted by exp(-energy/temperature), so as the temperature drops, only the best maps keep meaningful probability.
formal_definition: lambda(sigma) proportional to exp(-H(sigma)/T) (Eq. 13); as T tends to 0 it approaches a uniform distribution over minimum-energy states (compare the exponential distribution, Eq. 14, Fig 14).
why_it_matters: It converts 'find the minimum' into 'sample from this distribution at low temperature', which is exactly what MCMC methods know how to do.

label: Optimisation
plain_definition: Improving something step by step: repeatedly nudge the map, keep score, and steer towards the best score reachable.
formal_definition: Iteratively altering a mathematical circumstance so that a function acting on it takes on an extremal value (S2.2); here, navigating configurations to extremise an objective function.
why_it_matters: Once the rules are scores, boundary-drawing is optimisation; every method in the paper (Potts/MCMC, GA, annealing) is a strategy for doing this well at scale.

label: Multi-objective optimisation
plain_definition: Optimising several scores at once - fairness, counties, continuity, shape - which pull in different directions and must be traded against each other.
formal_definition: Combining per-rule objective functions into one overall function via weights (S2.8); faithfully translating a legal hierarchy into weights is itself an unsolved technical problem, as effects are not linear in the weights.
why_it_matters: Real redistricting is never one objective; the multi-objective structure is where all the genuine political trade-offs surface inside the mathematics.

label: Local minima
plain_definition: A map that cannot be improved by any single small change, yet is far from the best map overall - where naive step-by-step improvement gets stranded.
formal_definition: A configuration whose objective value is extremal within its move-neighbourhood but not globally; the paper motivates entertaining temporarily-worse configurations to avoid local minima (S2.3).
why_it_matters: Explains why the search must sometimes accept worse maps on the way to better ones - the intuition behind temperature and annealing.

label: Boundary-flip moves
plain_definition: The basic step of the search: pick an ED on a constituency border and try moving it into the neighbouring constituency, so constituencies morph and grow rather than scatter.
formal_definition: Restrict EDs eligible to change membership to those at constituency boundaries, flipping to a nearby constituency rather than a random one (S2.3); equivalently, reassigning one node at a time along district borders (S3.4).
why_it_matters: The move set determines what the search can reach and how fast; geographically informed moves are significantly faster than random reassignment.

label: Monte Carlo methods
plain_definition: Estimating a quantity by averaging over many random samples instead of computing it exactly - like estimating an average by polling rather than a full census.
formal_definition: Numerical algorithms involving random sampling used to calculate expected values; by the strong law of large numbers the sample mean of i.i.d. draws converges to the true mean (Eqs 24-25).
why_it_matters: Random sampling is the only viable way to learn anything about a space of more than 10^5000 maps.

label: Markov chain
plain_definition: A random sequence of states where the next step depends only on where you are now, not on how you got there.
formal_definition: A sequence of random variables where P(A_{N+1} | A_N, ..., A_0) = P(A_{N+1} | A_N), time-homogeneous (Eq. 26).
why_it_matters: The chain structure is what lets a simple local move rule, iterated, produce samples with a known, controllable distribution.

label: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)
plain_definition: A random walk through the space of maps, designed so that the maps it visits are samples from a chosen target distribution.
formal_definition: Methods forming a Markov chain on the state space whose stationary distribution is the desired distribution, so collected states constitute samples from it; the natural districting walk reassigns one unit at a time along borders (S3.4, App D).
why_it_matters: MCMC is the paper's chosen engine for both optimising maps and generating ensembles, with mixing theorems and convergence diagnostics as its theoretical backing.

label: Detailed balance
plain_definition: A pairwise fairness condition on the walk: the flow of probability from map A to map B equals the flow from B to A. A walk with this property provably settles into the target distribution.
formal_definition: t(sigma', sigma) lambda(sigma) = t(sigma, sigma') lambda(sigma') for all pairs (Eq. 29); it implies lambda is the equilibrium distribution of the transition kernel t.
why_it_matters: It is the guarantee that the sampling is principled rather than hopeful - the mathematical warrant behind trusting MCMC output.

label: Metropolis-Hastings algorithm
plain_definition: A recipe for building a valid walk: propose a change, then accept it with a cleverly chosen probability; the accept rule is engineered so detailed balance holds automatically.
formal_definition: Given proposal density p(sigma', sigma), accept with probability a = min(p(sigma,sigma') lambda(sigma') / (p(sigma',sigma) lambda(sigma)), 1) (Eq. 30); then t = a p satisfies detailed balance for lambda (Eqs 31-32).
why_it_matters: It is the master template: both algorithms actually run in the paper (Metropolis and Gibbs) are special cases of this one construction.

label: Metropolis algorithm
plain_definition: The workhorse special case: propose moving one ED to a random other constituency; if the map's energy drops, accept; if it rises, accept anyway with probability exp(-rise/temperature).
formal_definition: Metropolis-Hastings with a symmetric proposal, so a = min(exp(-Delta H / T), 1) (Eq. 34); only the energy change Delta H of the single-site update is needed; uniform proposal over the other Q-1 constituencies (Eq. 35). Steps boxed in S4.1.1.
why_it_matters: This is the actual update loop of the electoral Potts search: cheap to compute, provably samples the Boltzmann distribution, and easy to explain step by step.

label: Gibbs sampler
plain_definition: The always-accept variant: for one ED, compute the energy change for every possible constituency it could join, then pick among them with probabilities weighted by those changes.
formal_definition: Metropolis-Hastings with proposal p proportional to the target itself, giving acceptance probability exactly 1 (Eqs 36-38); the proposal over q = 1..Q is exp(-Delta H(q)/T) normalised. Steps boxed in S4.1.1.
why_it_matters: The paper's second sampler: costlier per step (Q energy evaluations) but never wastes a proposal - a concrete engineering trade-off against Metropolis.

label: Simulated annealing
plain_definition: Start the search hot and adventurous, then cool it slowly so it gradually commits to the best region it has found - like metal being annealed to remove defects.
formal_definition: Sampling from the temperature-dependent equilibrium distribution while T is slowly reduced from high to low, so the walk tracks equilibrium down to the global-extremum-dominated regime (S4.2.1, Fig 15); after Kirkpatrick et al. 1983.
why_it_matters: It is the technique that turns a sampler into an optimiser, and both of the paper's methods (Potts/MCMC and SAGA) rely on it.

label: Ensembles of comparison plans
plain_definition: Instead of judging a proposed map in isolation, generate thousands of alternative valid maps under the same rules and see where the proposal sits among them.
formal_definition: Large, diverse collections of valid plans sampled from the space of alternatives that cut the same jurisdiction by the same rules; inferences drawn from ensembles rely heavily on the distributions from which they are sampled (S3.4).
why_it_matters: Ensembles are how algorithmic output becomes evidence: they give the commission and the public a baseline of what maps are possible, not just one answer.

label: Genetic algorithm
plain_definition: A search inspired by evolution: keep a population of candidate maps, rank them by fitness, let the best ones breed and mutate, and repeat generation after generation.
formal_definition: A three-step loop - rank a population by fitness, preferentially select top individuals to breed, and form the next generation - where each individual is a configuration assigning every ED one of Q values (S4.1.2).
why_it_matters: It is the paper's second, independent search strategy, showing the framework is not tied to one algorithm: any method that optimises the codified rules can plug in.

label: Fitness function (GA)
plain_definition: The GA's score for a map, combining a compactness reward (built from counting same-constituency neighbour connections) and a population-balance reward, each with its own weight.
formal_definition: F = gamma_comp D + gamma_pop P (Eq. 15), with D = kappa arcsin(E/E_tot) for same-allocation adjacent edge count E, kappa = 50/3 (Eq. 16), and P = (1 - (2/pi) arctan((1/Q) sum |P_i/P_avg - 1|))^eta with harshness eta = 5 (Eq. 17); maximised rather than minimised.
why_it_matters: A second concrete codification of the same rules - comparing it with the Hamiltonian teaches that the encoding, not just the algorithm, is a design choice.

label: SAGA (simulated annealing genetic algorithm)
plain_definition: The paper's custom hybrid: a genetic algorithm whose mutation and selection run under a slowly cooling temperature, combining evolution's breadth with annealing's discipline.
formal_definition: A custom method combining the genetic algorithm layout with a simulated-annealing control regime; temperature decreases geometrically, T_k = 0.99^k T_0, with an initial population of size 2 and mutation by random ED reassignment (S4.1.2; the draft section is incomplete).
why_it_matters: It demonstrates that the framework's components (encoding, fitness, cooling) compose freely - and its small-scale results are half of the paper's proof of concept.

label: Hard vs soft constraints
plain_definition: Some rules may never be broken in a final map (seat total, 3-5 seats, contiguity); others (county lines, geography, continuity) can be - and in practice always are - bent to some degree.
formal_definition: Of the terms of reference, items (i) total seats, (ii) seat range and (iv) contiguity cannot be broken, whereas (iii) county boundaries, (v) geographic considerations and (vi) continuity can and will be transgressed to some extent (S1).
why_it_matters: This split structures the whole optimisation: hard constraints get prohibitive energy weights, soft ones get finite weights that encode how much bending is tolerable.

label: The constraint hierarchy problem
aliases: ranking the rules;relative importance of constraints
plain_definition: The law lists the soft objectives but never ranks them; it is only generally understood that equal representation trumps the rest. Yet any concrete map implicitly ranks them anyway.
formal_definition: No statutory statement of relative importance exists among county boundaries, geographic considerations and continuity (S1); translating any assumed hierarchy into an algorithm is a separate, additional problem (S2.8, S3.3).
why_it_matters: This is the gap the coupling constants fill - and the reason the paper insists the filling must be explicit, debatable and auditable rather than hidden in a committee room.

label: The variance vs county trade-off
plain_definition: Tighter fairness bounds leave less freedom to respect county lines. Example: Laois and Offaly together deserve 6 seats, but neither county alone can form a valid 3-seat constituency within ±5 percent - so something must give.
formal_definition: Increasing the acceptable variance threshold above ±5 percent facilitates smaller population transfers and fewer county-boundary disruptions; the tighter the variance bound, the less mathematical flexibility remains for the terms of reference (App C.2).
why_it_matters: It is the cleanest proof that the objectives genuinely conflict - no cleverness dissolves the tension, so a value judgement about the trade-off is unavoidable.

label: Proportionality vs local access
plain_definition: Bigger constituencies give smaller parties a fairer shot at the ballot box, but let elected TDs cluster in one corner of a large area, leaving parts of it without a nearby representative during the term.
formal_definition: Larger seat magnitude yields greater resolution of the electorate's political distribution, while demonstrably enabling disproportionate geographical clustering of representatives within constituencies; the paper poses this as an open, perhaps unresolvable tension of PR with constituency-based systems (S3.7).
why_it_matters: It reframes seat magnitude - normally a technical parameter - as a genuine democratic dilemma the reader can hold an informed opinion on.

label: Choosing among valid boundaries
aliases: process A and B;selecting the final map
plain_definition: Even after invalid maps are discarded, many valid ones remain. Two further steps happen: sorting boundaries into acceptable and not (which encodes interpretation), and then picking the single map to recommend.
formal_definition: Process A: sorting the solution space of boundaries into acceptable and unacceptable, dependent on one's interpretation of the rule set; Process B: selecting from the acceptable set the boundary to be recommended or implemented (S3.2, S3.6). No auditable trail of these steps currently exists.
why_it_matters: The final choice is where discretion lives today; making A and B explicit is what would let the public scrutinise why this map rather than that one.

label: Exploring the parameter space
plain_definition: Since no one can derive the right weights from first principles, you run the algorithm across many weight combinations and study how the resulting maps change.
formal_definition: Determining coupling constants reduces to investigating the behaviour and results of the algorithms for a variety of values of each constant (S2.8); the dedicated sections (S4.2.2, S5.2.2) are placeholders in the draft.
why_it_matters: Weight sweeps turn a hidden value judgement into an experiment whose results anyone can inspect: 'if you care more about counties, here is what your map looks like'.

label: Pareto frontier
plain_definition: The shortlist of maps you cannot improve in one respect without worsening another. Maps not on this frontier are simply beaten; maps on it differ only in values, not in quality.
formal_definition: A configuration is Pareto-optimal if no other configuration is at least as good on every objective and strictly better on one; the Pareto frontier is the set of such non-dominated configurations. Standard multi-objective optimisation theory; the paper does not use the term.
why_it_matters: It gives the commission and public the honest menu: algorithms can compute the frontier, but choosing a point on it is irreducibly a political decision.

label: Multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA)
plain_definition: A family of structured methods for choosing among options that are each scored on several criteria - making the weighing-up explicit instead of intuitive.
formal_definition: Formal methods (weighted scoring, outranking, and related techniques) for ranking or selecting alternatives evaluated against multiple, conflicting criteria. Standard decision-analysis material; the paper describes the selection problem (S3.2, S3.6) but does not name MCDA.
why_it_matters: It is the natural formal home for the paper's process B: once valid maps and their scores exist, MCDA is how a final recommendation can be made auditable.

label: Transparency and auditability
plain_definition: Today's review reports state outcomes but not the search path - which options were weighed and why. An algorithmic pipeline leaves a trail anyone can check and re-run.
formal_definition: The paper argues computational methods can provide an auditable trail for decisions and notes there is yet to be a trail outlining the steps or choices made between review inputs and recommended boundaries (S1.1, S3.2).
why_it_matters: Trust in boundaries should not require trusting the people who drew them; it can rest on being able to check the process itself.

label: Interpretability (no black box)
plain_definition: The framework deliberately uses a small number of dials, each of which can be debated in plain terms - and deliberately avoids black-box AI whose reasoning cannot be examined.
formal_definition: The algorithmic solution must be interpretable and open to scrutiny, using a minimal number of tunable parameters such that each parameter's value can be subject to legal debate; deep-learning approaches with thousands of non-linearly interdependent parameters are deliberately avoided (S1).
why_it_matters: For a democratic instrument, being explainable is not a nice-to-have: a map is only as legitimate as the reasons that can be given for it.

label: Decision support, not decision making
plain_definition: The algorithm does not draw Ireland's boundaries; it gives the human commission speed, options and evidence. The CSO's algorithm-assisted definition of urban areas, with humans resolving edge cases, is the precedent.
formal_definition: The framework aims to improve transparency, turnaround times and efficiency as decision support for the Electoral Commission, which faces reviews of EU, local (LEA) and Dail boundaries; the most recent census used algorithms with a human in the loop as precedent (S1.1, S5.2.3, S6).
why_it_matters: It answers the reader's most natural objection - 'should a computer decide this?' - directly: no, and the framework is designed so it cannot.

label: Testing the rules themselves
plain_definition: Beyond drawing maps, the framework can answer what-if questions about the rules: what would allowing 6-seat constituencies do? Would a proposed rule set resist deliberate manipulation?
formal_definition: Use cases include assessing existing legal rules in achieving fair representation and testing the resilience of rules against gerrymandering (S1); the 2023 report itself flags the 3-5 seat limit as constraining and raises 6-seat constituencies as a research question (S3.3).
why_it_matters: Rules are designed systems, and designed systems behave in ways their designers do not expect; simulation lets the Oireachtas test electoral law before enacting it.

label: Normative choices vs mathematics
aliases: values in, maps out;fairness is normative
plain_definition: Mathematics never decides what fair means - people do. What the framework does is take a chosen definition of fairness and expose, precisely, what follows from it.
formal_definition: The paper makes no assertions about the correctness or morality of any districting solution and does not prescribe a definition of representation, which is inherently a normative concept; it provides tools to assess whether proposed rule sets lead to systems aligned with one's values (S6.1).
why_it_matters: Keeping this boundary sharp is what makes the framework trustworthy: it clarifies that disagreement about maps is disagreement about values, now visible instead of hidden.

label: Democratic legitimacy
plain_definition: The end goal: every vote carrying as near as possible equal weight, produced by a process citizens can understand, check and contest - so that the map itself commands trust.
formal_definition: Equal representation realised through boundaries that respect the Constitution and terms of reference, produced by a transparent, auditable, scrutinisable process; the paper frames Ireland's challenge as refining an already functional and independent system, unlike jurisdictions battling gerrymandering (S1.1, S6).
why_it_matters: This is the 'so what' of the entire course: redistricting arithmetic is invisible plumbing, but it determines whether your vote counts the same as your neighbour's.
